title: Cohort-based sensitivity sweep and threshold hypersearch for quant profiles (AWQ/GPTQ)
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, cohort-driven evaluation and hypersearch pipeline that maps quantization profiles (AWQ/GPTQ, int8/int4) to per-cohort quality deltas and automatically proposes per-profile thresholds and gating policies. Motivation: existing single-threshold approaches mask large variance across prompt cohorts (conversational, retrieval-augmented, instruction-following). We need fine-grained thresholds so rollouts can maintain SLOs for critical cohorts while aggressively quantizing low-risk cohorts to reduce cost.

Success criteria:
- A hypersearch job can produce a sensitivity matrix (cohorts x metrics x bitwidth/profile) within 24h for a new model variant.
- Automated threshold suggestions that keep per-cohort metric regressions within configured SLAs (e.g., <1% EM drop for QA-critical cohorts, <0.5% hallucination increase for factual tasks).
- Integration with regression-monitoring to block deployments when cohort-level metrics exceed thresholds.

Approach:
1) Cohort definition: create stratified buckets based on prompt archetypes (short instructions, multi-turn chat, code, retrieval-augmented, high-precision QA). Buckets will be populated from production prompt logs and synthetic augmentations.
2) Metrics: use a mixed set: EM/F1 for QA, ROUGE/BLEU for summarization/translation, embedding-similarity (cosine) and MSE on logits for distribution drift, and a calibrated hallucination scorer for factual tasks.
3) Hypersearch: run parallel grid/random/hyperband searches across quant profiles (AWQ/GPTQ variants, per-layer granularity), temperature/act-ordering changes that affect quant sensitivity, and threshold candidates for gating. Early stopping based on cohort-specific stopping criteria to save cost.
4) Sensitivity matrix: output CSV and visualization that shows delta per metric vs baseline for each cohort/profile. Also compute a cost delta (tokens/sec and GPU-hr estimate) to enable cost-quality trade-off charts.
5) Threshold recommendations: algorithm will propose per-cohort thresholds using constrained optimization (minimize cost subject to metric constraints) and label each recommendation as conservative / balanced / aggressive.
6) Integration: push recommendations as metadata to model catalog, tag model variants with recommended gating rules, and create a regression-monitoring rule in Console that triggers if live cohort metrics exceed configured thresholds for X consecutive windows.

Deliverables:
- Evals harness job spec and runbook (Confluence)
- Sensitivity matrix artifacts and visualization in dashboards
- Threshold suggestion engine code and a small API endpoint for Console to fetch recommended gates
- Regression-monitoring rules for canary and global rollouts
- End-to-end test: run on model-rx-1.0 candidate quant profiles and verify canary behavior in staging

Risks and trade-offs:
- Run cost: exhaustive hypersearch across all cohorts and profiles is expensive. Mitigation: stratified sampling and adaptive search with early stopping.
- Metric misalignment: some business-critical metrics are hard to capture automatically (e.g., subjective instruction quality). Mitigation: flag cohorts as manually-reviewed-required and surface sample prompts for human checks.
- Overfitting thresholds to synthetic cohorts. Mitigation: holdout a portion of production prompts for validation.

Next steps:
- Finalize cohort definitions with PM and DS (due 2026-02-21).
- Implement initial hypersearch harness and run against model-rx-1.0 baseline (ETA: 2026-02-28).
- Add threshold optimizer and wire up Console preview (ETA: 2026-03-08).
